full_judgment:
6. The learned Judge of Special Tribunal after conclusion of trial considering the facts, circumstances and evidence on record passed the impugned judgment and order dated 31.10.1999 convicting the appellant under section 19 (A) of the Arms Act and sentencing him to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of 10 years. 

 8. Mr. Aminul Ahsan on behalf of Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, learned Advocates appearing for the convict appellant submits that prosecution examined 12 witnesses out of which 10 are police personnel and rest two were public witnesses. P.W. 1-5 cross-examined by the defence but P.W. 6,7, and 8 were tendered and defence declined to cross examined them. None of the public and seizure list witnesses supported the prosecution case. So, judgment and order of conviction and sentence are not sustainable in law. He further submits that even prosecution has failed to prove the case by adducing any independent and disinterested witnesses. He further referring the evidences of police witnesses pointing the contradictions in their evidences submits that only the police personnel supported the prosecution case and there are no reasons to belief them in the facts and circumstance of the case. He further submits that the learned Judge of Special Tribunal though has given the reasonings in support of prosecution case, however, those are not based on the evidence on record and as such the finding and decision of the tribunal are not sustainable in law. Therefore, the impugned Judgment and order of conviction is liable to be set aside. 

 9. On the other hand, Mr. Abdus Salam Mondol, the learned Deputy attorney General submits that the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence are well founded and based on material on record. He submits that out of 12 witnesses 10 witnesses proved the prosecution case by giving evidence beyond the all reasonable doubt. He further adds that all the official witnesses are disinterested and independent because they have no personal conflict with the accused and as such their testimonies are quote believable, thus, there is no reason to interfere with the finding and decision of the trial court. He next submits that informant along with other witnesses who accompanied him at the time of surrounding the house of the accused and recovered the Arms from his residence had consistently corroborated the prosecution case. There is no material contradictions and inconsistencies which created any doubt regarding prosecution case and as such the appeal is liable to be dismissed. 

 11. We have perused the judgment, memo of appeal, evidences and materials on record. 

 13. From the above evidence it is clear that testimonies of these witnesses directly contradict with the testimony of P.W.12 informant and investigation officer because he stated in reply to a question of defence that the house of accused Rezaul has been identified by the Chowkider whose name was not known to him. Police personnel made contradictory statement which create serious doubt about recovery of the arms and bullets as well as the credibility of their testimonies, therefore, prosecution case is highly doubtful and testimonies of the prosecution witnesses are unworthy of credit. Moreover, Investigating Officer, in reply to a question of defence in cross examination admitted that in the sketch map and index though he mentioned that there are some house adjacent to the house of accused but he failed to mention the name of the owner of those houses in his sketch map and index and those owners were not cited as witnesses in the charge sheet. It is presumed that had those persons examined in this case surely they would not have support the prosecution and as such the convict appellant is entitled to get the benefit of doubt under section 114 (g) of the Evidence Act. 

 "Considering the entire gamut of prosecution evidence I am convinced that these two seizure list witnesses being close neighbor of the accused have suppressed the facts of their presence at the time of recovery of arms from accused house." 

 15. We are unable to accept this observation of the learned Judge because of fact that in this case not only the seizure list witnesses disproof the prosecution case however, from the evidence of P.W.1, 2 and 12 as discussed' above who are the police personnel it crystal clear that evidence of those prosecution witnesses are full of discrepancies and inconsistencies which are unworthy of credit, the discrepancies in the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses are so fatal which render the prosecution case doubtful. 

 "The public witnesses did not support the prosecution case and the prosecution failed to come with reasonable explanation as to why they did not support the prosecution story nor any enmity with the informant of this case, so, the persistence evidences of the public witnesses regarding denial of their presence at the time of alleged recovery in no way can be cured by the official witnesses (Police Personnel) who are none but interested witnesses." 

 20. Considering the facts, circumstances and discussions made herein above we are of the view that the prosecution case is fully pregnant with the legends of surmise and conjecture as to the recovery of the arms and ammunitions from the possession and control of the convict appellant as alleged and that without sufficient reliable evidence mere surmise and conjecture are not enough to warrant conviction of the accused. The prosecution having failed to bring home the charge to the accused Md. Rejoul Haque @ Ezaul beyond all reasonable doubts he is entitled to benefit of doubt and as such liable to be acquitted of the charge. He is liable to be acquitted on the ground of benefit of doubt.
